title: Compiler Front-End
description: From characters to a typed tree: lexing, parsing, names, and the errors a compiler owes the human.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS143 Compilers
sourceReferences.notes: Lex, parse, semantic analysis as the first project phases. Optimization waits.

sourceReferences.title: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools
sourceReferences.notes: Regular lexers, CFGs, and the source-to-tree pipeline. Mechanism, not theorem lists.

modules.title: Lexical analysis
learningObjectives: Keep a span so a diagnostic can point

modules.title: Parsing
learningObjectives: Recover nested structure from a token stream
Drop punctuation into the tree typechecking will walk

modules.title: Names and types
learningObjectives: Bind each use to a declaration
Reject a tree whose operators cannot agree

concepts.name: Lexing and parsing
concepts.summary: Turning characters into a tree the rest of the compiler can hate.
objectives: Trace source text through lexing and parsing into a tree later stages can consume
Name what errors the front end can report before any IR exists

concepts.name: Tokens
concepts.summary: The words of a programming language.
objectives: Describe a token as a classified lexeme plus the payload later stages need
Split a short source fragment into the tokens a parser would see

concepts.name: Regular lexers
concepts.summary: Why identifiers and numbers are regular while nested expressions are not.
objectives: Explain why identifiers and numbers are regular while nested expressions are not
Predict which lexeme a maximal-munch lexer accepts at a given position

concepts.name: Source locations
concepts.summary: Every diagnostic needs a span.
objectives: Attach a source span to a token so a diagnostic can point at the original text
Predict what a diagnostic loses if tokens forget where they came from

concepts.name: Preprocessing
concepts.summary: A language before the language.
objectives: Describe preprocessing as a rewrite of the token stream before the language parser runs
Name an error that appears only after expansion, not in the raw source

concepts.name: Macros
concepts.summary: Expansion that later phases must still explain.
objectives: Trace a macro expansion and the token stream the parser actually sees
Explain why a later diagnostic must still mention the use site, not only the expansion

concepts.name: Context-free grammars
concepts.summary: Recursive structure you can write down.
objectives: Write a small context-free grammar that generates nested expressions
Distinguish a regular token language from a context-free phrase structure

concepts.name: Parse trees
concepts.summary: The derivation, including the punctuation.
objectives: Build the concrete parse tree for a short derivation, including punctuation
Name what the parse tree still contains that later stages do not need

concepts.name: Abstract syntax trees
concepts.summary: The tree you actually want to typecheck.
objectives: Drop concrete punctuation from a parse tree to obtain the AST typechecking will walk
Distinguish a parse tree from an AST on the same source fragment

concepts.name: Recursive descent
concepts.summary: One function per nonterminal.
objectives: Trace one function-per-nonterminal parse of a short token stream
Predict where a recursive-descent parser fails on left recursion

concepts.name: Bottom-up parsing
concepts.summary: Shift and reduce, and the tables that drive them.
objectives: Trace a short shift/reduce sequence on a tiny grammar
Diagnose a shift/reduce conflict as two legal actions on the same lookahead

concepts.name: Ambiguity
concepts.summary: Two trees for one string.
objectives: Exhibit two different trees for one string under an ambiguous grammar
Resolve a classic ambiguity with precedence or a rewritten production

concepts.name: LL versus LR
concepts.summary: What each algorithm will not swallow.
objectives: Predict a construct LL cannot swallow that LR still can
Compare what left recursion and left factoring do to each algorithm

concepts.name: Semantic actions
concepts.summary: Building values while you parse.
objectives: Describe a semantic action as a value built while a production is recognized
Predict the AST node a reduction or a descent return constructs

concepts.name: Parse error recovery
concepts.summary: Reporting more than the first mistake.
objectives: Explain how panic-mode recovery reports more than the first bad token
Predict where a recursive-descent parser resynchronizes after a missing semicolon

concepts.name: Symbol tables
concepts.summary: A map from names to meanings, stacked by scope.
objectives: Describe a symbol table as a stacked map from names to declarations
Predict what a lookup returns after a new scope is pushed

concepts.name: Scope
concepts.summary: Where a name is visible.
objectives: State where a name is visible and where a hole or shadow hides it
Predict which declaration an inner use sees when an outer name is shadowed

concepts.name: Name resolution
concepts.summary: Which declaration this use refers to.
objectives: Bind a use to exactly one declaration using the active scope stack
Diagnose an unbound name as a resolution failure, not a parse failure

concepts.name: Type checking
concepts.summary: Rejecting trees that cannot mean anything.
objectives: Reject a well-parsed tree whose operators and operands cannot agree
Predict the type of a small expression after names have been resolved

concepts.name: Overload resolution
concepts.summary: Picking which f this f is.
objectives: Pick the unique viable candidate for a call given argument types
Diagnose an ambiguous call as more than one equally good candidate

concepts.name: Walking the tree
concepts.summary: Visitors and the passes that share them.
objectives: Walk an AST with a visitor so several passes share one traversal shape
Name what a later pass may assume after an earlier walk has finished

concepts.name: Lowering, first look
concepts.summary: The typed tree is not yet something you can allocate registers for.
objectives: Explain why a typed tree is still not a form you can allocate registers for
Name what lowering must make explicit before three-address code exists
